figures.cap: directed road network with minimum cut

parts.latex:
The diagram below shows a network of directed roads on which vehicles travel from a shopping centre at S to a car park at P. The maximum capacity (vehicles per hour) is shown, and the minimum cut is shown as the dashed line.

\exfigure{2846_q7b_1}
How many possible paths are there through the network of roads from S to P?
Explain why the capacity of the minimum cut is 800 vehicles per hour.

solutions.latex:
The minimum cut passes through edges $AC$, $DC$ and $FP$, so its capacity is the sum of their capacities.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Min cut} &= 200 + 300 + 300 \\ &= 800 \text{ vehicles per hour} \end{aligned}$$
